title: Essentially of finite type ring maps
statement: Let $\varphi:R\to S$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings. For a commutative $R$-algebra $B$ and a multiplicative subset $W\subseteq B$ ($1\in W$, $st\in W$ for $s,t\in W$) let $W^{-1}B$ be the ring of fractions $b/w$ ($b\in B$, $w\in W$; $b/w=b'/w'$ iff $u(bw'-b'w)=0$ for some $u\in W$), an $R$-algebra through $R\to B\to W^{-1}B$, $b\mapsto b/1$. The ring map $\varphi$ is *essentially of finite type*, or $S$ is an $R$-algebra *essentially of finite type*, if there are an $R$-algebra $B$ of finite type [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], a multiplicative subset $W\subseteq B$ and an isomorphism of $R$-algebras $S\cong W^{-1}B$.
